quick: 50 mg ~1 hr before sexual activity (range 30 min-4 hr); range 25-100 mg, max once/day
May take with or without food; a high-fat meal delays absorption (Tmax +60 min, Cmax -29%)
Not indicated in females; no human pregnancy data
Not indicated in females; small amounts in breast milk
Severe impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min): consider starting 25 mg; no adjustment for mild/moderate
Any degree of impairment (Child-Pugh A/B): consider starting 25 mg; not studied in Child-Pugh C
No potentiation of hypotension at moderate intake; additive vasodilation possible with excess
Blood pressure, cardiovascular status; vision/hearing changes; prolonged erection
summary: Sildenafil is an oral PDE5 inhibitor indicated for the treatment of erectile dysfunction. The usual dose is 50 mg taken about 1 hour (range 30 minutes to 4 hours) before sexual activity, adjustable to a maximum of 100 mg or minimum of 25 mg, no more than once daily. It is absolutely contraindicated with nitrates and with guanylate cyclase stimulators such as riociguat because of life-threatening hypotension. Notable risks include hypotension, non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION), sudden hearing loss, and priapism.
indications: Treatment of erectile dysfunction (ED) in adult males

dosage.d: 50 mg as needed, approximately 1 hour before sexual activity
dosage.t: May be taken 30 minutes to 4 hours before activity; maximum once per day
dosage.n: Titrate to 100 mg (max) or 25 mg (min) based on efficacy and tolerability

dosage.t: Ensure patient is stable on alpha-blocker before starting sildenafil
dosage.n: Additive blood-pressure lowering; use lowest dose
Strong CYP3A4 inhibition markedly raises levels

dosage.c: With strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or erythromycin
dosage.d: Consider a starting dose of 25 mg
dosage.t: Applies to ketoconazole, itraconazole, saquinavir, erythromycin

dosage.c: Age >65, hepatic impairment, or severe renal impairment
dosage.d: Consider a starting dose of 25 mg
dosage.t: Higher plasma levels in these populations

admin: Take one dose orally about 1 hour before anticipated sexual activity (anywhere from 30 minutes to 4 hours before)
Requires sexual stimulation to be effective
May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal can delay onset
Do not exceed one dose in a 24-hour period
Available as 25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg film-coated tablets
moa: Penile erection requires nitric oxide (NO) release in the corpus cavernosum during sexual stimulation, which activates guanylate cyclase to raise cyclic GMP (cGMP), causing smooth muscle relaxation and inflow of blood. Sildenafil selectively inhibits phosphodiesterase type 5 (PDE5), the enzyme that degrades cGMP, thereby increasing cGMP and enhancing the NO-mediated erectile response. It has no direct relaxant effect and no effect in the absence of sexual stimulation.

absolute: Concurrent use of nitric oxide donors / organic nitrates or nitrites in any form (regular or intermittent) - potentiates hypotension
Concurrent guanylate cyclase (GC) stimulators such as riociguat - additive hypotension
Known hypersensitivity to sildenafil or any component of the tablet
relative: Conditions in which sexual activity is inadvisable due to cardiovascular status
Anatomic penile deformation or conditions predisposing to priapism (sickle cell anemia, multiple myeloma, leukemia)
History of NAION (use only when benefits outweigh risks) or 'crowded' optic disc
Resting hypotension (BP <90/50), uncontrolled hypertension (BP >170/110), recent MI/stroke/arrhythmia within 6 months, unstable angina, or heart failure
Retinitis pigmentosa; bleeding disorders or active peptic ulceration
monitor: Blood pressure, especially with alpha-blockers or antihypertensives

preg: Sildenafil is not indicated for use in females. There are no human data to inform drug-associated risk in pregnancy. Animal reproduction studies in rats and rabbits showed no teratogenicity, embryotoxicity, or fetotoxicity at oral doses up to ~16x and ~32x the maximum recommended human dose (100 mg/day) on a mg/m2 basis.
lact: Sildenafil is not indicated for use in females. Limited data indicate sildenafil and its active metabolite are present in human milk; there is no information on effects on the breastfed child or on milk production.
renal: No dose adjustment for mild (CrCl 50-80 mL/min) or moderate (CrCl 30-49 mL/min) renal impairment. For severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min), clearance is reduced (~2-fold higher exposure); consider a starting dose of 25 mg.
hepatic: In hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh A and B), clearance is reduced with higher exposure (Cmax +47%, AUC +85%); consider a starting dose of 25 mg. Pharmacokinetics in severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh C) have not been studied.

major: Organic nitrates / nitric oxide donors (nitroglycerin, isosorbide, amyl nitrite) - CONTRAINDICATED; severe hypotension
Guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat) - CONTRAINDICATED; additive hypotension
Ritonavir (strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) - ~11-fold increase in sildenafil AUC; limit to 25 mg per 48 hours
moderate: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, saquinavir) - increased sildenafil exposure; start at 25 mg
Erythromycin - ~160-182% increase in Cmax/AUC; start at 25 mg
Alpha-blockers - additive hypotension; ensure stable on alpha-blocker and start sildenafil at 25 mg
Antihypertensives including amlodipine - additive BP reduction (~8/7 mmHg with amlodipine)
Other PDE5 inhibitors or other ED/PAH therapies (including REVATIO) - not recommended; additive BP lowering
minor: Anticoagulants/aspirin - postmarketing bleeding reports; causality not established
interactions.food: May be taken with or without food; a high-fat meal reduces absorption rate (mean Tmax delayed ~60 min, Cmax reduced ~29%).
interactions.alcohol: At moderate intake (alcohol 0.5 g/kg with sildenafil 50 mg) sildenafil did not potentiate alcohol's hypotensive effect; both are vasodilators, so excessive alcohol may add to BP lowering.
interactions.diagnostics: No routine lab monitoring required; assess cardiovascular status before prescribing.

common: Abnormal/color-tinged vision, light sensitivity, blurred vision
serious: Symptomatic hypotension and syncope (especially with nitrates, alpha-blockers, or antihypertensives)
Non-arteritic anterior ischemic optic neuropathy (NAION) - sudden vision loss
Sudden decrease or loss of hearing, with tinnitus and dizziness
Serious cardiovascular/cerebrovascular events (MI, sudden cardiac death, arrhythmia, stroke)
rare: Seizure / seizure recurrence, transient global amnesia
Vaso-occlusive crisis in sickle cell disease
Retinal vascular disease/bleeding, vitreous detachment, diplopia
emergency: Erection lasting longer than 4 hours - seek immediate medical attention (priapism risk)
Sudden loss of vision in one or both eyes - stop drug and seek care (possible NAION)
Sudden decrease or loss of hearing - stop drug and seek prompt care
Chest pain, severe dizziness, or fainting during/after sexual activity
Severe hypotension after taking with nitrates

monitoring: Cardiovascular assessment before prescribing (rule out conditions where sexual activity is inadvisable)
Blood pressure, particularly when combined with alpha-blockers or antihypertensives
Vision changes (sudden loss may signal NAION)
Erection duration (>4 hours warrants emergency care)
counsel: Take about 1 hour before sex (may work 30 minutes to 4 hours before); requires sexual stimulation to be effective
NEVER use with nitrate medications (e.g., nitroglycerin, isosorbide) or recreational nitrites ('poppers') - can cause dangerous drops in blood pressure
Do not use with riociguat (a guanylate cyclase stimulator)
Use no more than once per day
A high-fat meal may delay how quickly it works
Seek emergency care for an erection lasting more than 4 hours
Stop the drug and seek care for sudden vision loss or sudden hearing loss
Sildenafil does not protect against sexually transmitted diseases including HIV
Tell your doctor about heart disease, recent heart attack/stroke, low or high blood pressure, and all medicines including alpha-blockers
pk: Within ~30-60 minutes; effect requires sexual stimulation
Plasma Tmax 30-120 min (median 60 min) fasted; bioavailability ~41%
Terminal half-life ~4 hours (parent and active metabolite)
Up to ~4 hours of effective window after dosing
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions permitted 15-30 C (59-86 F)
pearls: Absolutely contraindicated with nitrates in any form and with guanylate cyclase stimulators (riociguat) - life-threatening hypotension
After a dose, the safe interval before nitrates can be given (if needed) is unknown - a major consideration in emergency chest pain
Start at 25 mg in patients on alpha-blockers, ritonavir/strong CYP3A4 inhibitors, age >65, severe renal impairment, or hepatic impairment
Counsel to stop the drug and seek care for sudden vision or hearing loss (NAION and ototoxicity reports)
Erection >4 hours is a urologic emergency (priapism) that can cause permanent damage
A high-fat meal delays onset (Cmax -29%, Tmax +60 min); take on a relatively empty stomach for faster effect
missed: Sildenafil is used as needed, not on a fixed schedule, so there is no missed-dose concern. Take a dose only when planning sexual activity and never take more than one dose in a 24-hour period.
overdose: In single doses up to 800 mg, adverse reactions were similar to those at lower doses but more frequent and severe (e.g., headache, flushing, hypotension, syncope, visual disturbance, prolonged erection). Management is standard supportive care. Renal dialysis is not expected to accelerate clearance because sildenafil is highly protein-bound and not eliminated in the urine.
